summary: The root قطمر (qTmr) refers to the thin skin or cleft of a date-stone, or the small white point from which a palm tree grows. It metaphorically signifies something small, mean, or paltry.
lane: قِطْمِيرٌ ذ (S, K) and قِطْمَارٌ (K) The cleft ( شَقّ ) of a date-stone: (M, K:) or the integument ( قِشْرَة ) that is upon it ( فِيهَا ): (K:) the thin skin (S, K) called فُوفَة , which is upon a date-stone, (S,) between the stone and the date itself: (K:) or the white point [i. e. the embryo ] in the back of the date-stone, (S, K,) from which [ when it is sown ] the palm-tree grows forth. (S.) -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) A small, mean, paltry, contemptible, thing. So the former signifies in the Kur, xxxv. 14. One says also مَا أَصَبْتُ مِنْهُ قِطْمِيرًا , meaning, (assumed tropical:) I obtained not of him, or it, anything. (TA.)

entries.text: القطمير : الذي تعلق به النواة مع القمع إذا أخرجتها من التمر.
القِطْميرُ: الفوفَةُ التي في النواة، وهي القشرةُ الرقيقةُ، ويقال هي النُكتة البيضاء التي في ظهر النواة تنبت منها النخلة.
قال تعالى: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ ما يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْ قِطْمِيرٍ﴾ [فاطر : 13] أي: الأثر في ظهر النّواة، وذلك مثل للشيء الطّفيف.

قطمر: القِطْمِيرُ والقِطْمارُ: شَقُّ النَّوَاةِ، وَفِي الصِّحَاحِ: القِطْمِيرُ الفُوفة الَّتِي فِي النَّوَاةِ، وَهِيَ القِشْرة الدَّقِيقَةُ الَّتِي عَلَى النَّوَاةِ بَيْنَ النَّوَاةِ وَالتَّمْرِ، وَيُقَالُ: هِيَ النُّكْتة الْبَيْضَاءُ الَّتِي فِي ظَهْرِ النَّوَاةِ الَّتِي تَنْبُتُ مِنْهَا النَّخْلَةُ. وَمَا أَصبتُ مِنْهُ قِطْميراً أَي شيئاً.

classical_note: Arabic-only entries from public-domain classical lexica, ordered by compiler death date. Tier 'root-semantic' (Maqayis) derives all senses of a root from one core idea. Tier 'interpretive' (Mufradat) cites hadith and takes theological positions and is not equivalent evidence. Tier 'earliest-disputed' (Kitab al-Ayn) marks a text whose attribution to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad (d. 786) is contested: the work itself records that his student al-Layth ibn al-Muzaffar completed it after his death, so the 786 date orders the entry but does not assert sole authorship. Kitab al-Ayn is arranged by point of articulation, not alphabetically, and files geminate roots with two letters; the al-Ayn headword actually used is preserved in each entry.
